good.title: Tidal power
good.lead: Tidal power converts the regular rise and fall of the sea, driven mainly by the moon's gravity, into electricity. Plants capture the energy with barrages, lagoons or underwater turbines, and their output is predictable because tides follow astronomical cycles.
good.body_md:
## Principle

Tides are caused by the gravitational pull of the moon and, to a lesser extent, the sun on the oceans, which raises and lowers the sea surface twice a day in most places [1]. The difference between high and low water is the tidal range, and it varies from a few centimetres in open oceans to more than ten metres in some funnel-shaped bays. A tidal power plant turns the potential energy of that height difference, or the kinetic energy of the moving water, into electricity with turbines and a generator.

## Technologies

A tidal barrage is a dam built across an estuary. Gates let the incoming tide fill the basin, and the stored water is released through turbines as the tide falls, and in some designs also as it rises [2]. The best known example is the Rance tidal power station in Brittany, France, which has operated since 1966 [2]. A tidal lagoon works in a similar way but impounds water behind a sea wall built out from the coast rather than across a river mouth, which leaves the estuary open [3]. Tidal stream generators resemble wind turbines placed on the seabed, where fast currents turn their blades; they need no dam, but they must withstand strong forces and marine growth.

## Characteristics

Tides follow astronomical cycles, so the output of a plant can be forecast years ahead, unlike wind and solar power. Output is not constant, however: it peaks twice a day and varies over the fortnightly spring and neap cycle, so tidal plants need storage or other sources to supply steady demand [1]. Building a barrage or a lagoon is expensive and changes local ecosystems, sediment movement and navigation, and these effects, together with the high cost for each unit of capacity, have limited the number of large plants worldwide [2][3].

## Key facts

- Tides are caused mainly by the gravitational pull of the moon [1]
- The Rance tidal power station in France opened in 1966 and still operates [2]
- A tidal lagoon impounds water behind a sea wall instead of damming a river mouth [3]
- Tidal output can be forecast years ahead but varies through each day and the spring and neap cycle [1][3]

work_verification.about: WORK 4.3, 4.4: events are attest (an agreeing attestation from a pair distinct from every earlier one), window_end, refetch_ok (the server fetched a copy within simhash_max of a group) and refetch_fail. verified_by is whose text is indexed; frontier_row is the pool entry class frontier or errored row, null for pushed. state, verified_by, indexed_text and frontier_row describe the end of the path on the assumption that moderation (WORK 4.5) allows the page and IndexAttested (WORK 6.4) succeeds: a deferral, a rejection or an index failure leaves indexed_text null and the row as it was, and WORK 4.1 completes the row only after IndexAttested.
